summary_responses.response: The FCC issued a Paperwork Reduction Act notice seeking public and interagency comments by December 7, 2026, on revised information-collection requirements tied to its Upper C-band (3.98–4.14 GHz) transition and related 3.7 GHz processes. The collections support a July 22, 2026 FCC order aimed at clearing incumbent fixed-satellite service operations so 160 MHz can be auctioned for flexible terrestrial wireless use by July 4, 2027, with clearing deadlines extending to December 30, 2030 or June 30, 2031. For OMB Control No. 3060-1275, the FCC estimates 16,512 respondents, 34,871 responses, 123,465 annual burden hours, and about $10.7 million in annual costs, covering reporting, recordkeeping, and disclosures. The plan creates an independent Upper C-band Clearinghouse to administer reimbursements, lump-sum and incentive payments, and FAA-related radio-altimeter retrofit rebates, and a Relocation Coordinator to manage engineering, scheduling, and dispute resolution for earth-station migrations. Eligible space station operators must file transition plans and quarterly status updates, submit certifications of completion to qualify for incentives, and promptly report any delays, while the FCC also seeks PRA approval for a separate revised collection (OMB 3060-1281) covering 3.7 GHz service licensee/earth-station agreements and engineering analyses.

summary_responses.response: The article describes DiffTry (Differential Retries), a proposed change to retry behavior in microservice architectures that turns retries into a distributed rejection-prioritization mechanism during overload. Instead of using a single retry limit for all requests, DiffTry assigns class-specific retry budgets (e.g., more retries for premium/high-priority requests and fewer for low-priority or potentially malicious traffic), requiring no overload detection, coordination between services, or application changes. The authors argue this both protects valuable transactions during miscoordination-induced overload and suppresses “retry storms” that can worsen performance and cost. They develop analytical models for a simple two-service tandem case and then extend the analysis to general microservice networks, providing convergence/uniqueness results (especially for DAG-shaped service graphs) and monotonicity guarantees as retry limits increase. Simulations and a live Kubernetes service-mesh plugin deployment show the measured rejection and prioritization effects closely match the theory, with high-priority traffic seeing substantially lower rejection and higher share of successful completions under overload.

summary_responses.response: The Office of Personnel Management issued a direct final rule to make technical updates to its title 5 Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) regulations to match statutory amendments enacted in January 2021 and December 2023. The rule also confirms that employees may substitute annual and sick leave provided under authorities outside title 5 for otherwise unpaid FMLA leave, consistent with existing regulatory language. In addition, it removes certain Veterans Health Administration employees who are covered by VA’s separate leave system under 38 U.S.C. 7421 from title 5 FMLA coverage and clarifies that OPM’s title 5 FMLA rules do not apply to them. The rule will take effect December 14, 2026 unless OPM receives significant adverse comments by November 16, 2026, in which case OPM will withdraw the affected parts and proceed with a proposed rule.
